title: Temperature differences gave no clear taxon overlap link in four British beetle samples in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether absolute temperature differences between consecutive years predict less overlap of caught beetle taxa. We used 591 matched location-month pairs in England and Scotland in two periods, with source years 1993-2003 and 2004-2015. A ratio of expected shared taxa to expected richness held catch size fixed at 20 individuals. Models controlled location by month, year, rain, effort and date differences. Fixed-size deficit slopes were +0.0097, -0.0084, +0.0305 and +0.0105 per C. All four corrected year-cluster intervals included zero. Raw-minus-fixed slope intervals also included zero. Fixed samples of 10 and 30 individuals did not give clear slopes. Few Scottish pairs, coarse weather, shared years and selected catches limit inference. The outcome includes sampling variation and does not measure true local turnover. We test no causal warming or pollution effect. The package gives code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, checks and a figure. External raw and derived record tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Overlap-deficit slopes for absolute year-to-year temperature differences. All corrected intervals include zero. Fixed catch size does not remove taxon capture bias.

citations.reason: We adapt its published collection construction and retrieval code and use the same source archive. Our between-year taxon overlap outcome differs from its within-collection richness test.
